verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents 24 official SDKs spanning backend (Python, server-side inline experiments), web (JS, React, Vue, script tag, Cloudflare edge) and mobile (Kotlin/Android, Swift/iOS, Flutter, React Native). It states that all SDKs share the same assignment logic, backed by a language-agnostic test suite of over 400 cases. The 2021 community remark about lacking native mobile SDKs predates and is superseded by the current Kotlin and Swift SDK docs, so it is not a live contradiction. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that flag evaluation is consistent across multiple SDKs, and feature-parity detail (e.g. streaming is limited to JavaScript and React).

support.subject: As a developer, I can use official SDKs across my whole stack — backend, web, and mobile — with consistent flag behavior

citations.quote: 24 SDKs including React, Python, Android, and iOS.
All SDKs use the same assignment logic, so the same attributes always produce the same variation regardless of which SDK you use.
an extensive test suite with over 400 language-agnostic unit tests in JSON format
Install the GrowthBook Kotlin SDK to evaluate feature flags and run A/B tests in Android apps using Android SDK 21 and above.
Install the GrowthBook Swift SDK to evaluate feature flags and run A/B tests on iOS, macOS, tvOS, and other Apple platforms.
This SDK supports both ReactJS and ReactNative environments and both client and server components.
